grounding.quote:

record identities are unique across their disjoint union. Let `Local_M` be

member of `External_M` is admitted only through one signature-declared
external reference domain and exact resolution relation. A hidden record,
an unpopulated extra record family, an identity occurring in two
populations, or an identity in `I` with neither one local record nor one
lawful external resolution refuses the model. A population may be empty
only when the selected signature does not require a member of that record
kind (P3, P5).

coerced to satisfied (P5, P6). The
core values, the rule that no mapping raises a result's standing and the

judgment of a constraint and to the outcomes of the operations of this

Every `a_c` signature imports those identities unchanged. A model-family

admissible kinds; it does not remove, rename, shadow or silently add a

constraints.statement: Import all eight core identities unchanged; family signatures specialise fields/domains/kinds without removing, renaming, shadowing or silently adding families. Unknown kinds/fields require a new signature or explicit compatible extension, not implicit extension or extra subject sort. Populations are finite, total, disjoint and identity-unique; every record belongs exactly once and every external identity has exactly one declared reference domain/resolution. Hidden records, extra unpopulated families, duplicate identities or identities lacking local record/lawful external resolution refuse the model. Every identity-bearing scalar/collection element is checked by RefDomain_Sigma: exact family, semantic sort where applicable, and exact external kind/basis; never both local and external. Missing field domains, wrong families/sorts, ambiguous targets and dangling external identities refuse structural admission.
exceptions: A population may be empty only when the selected signature requires no member of that kind.
A new fundamental family requires an explicit compatible calculus extension.

grounding.quote:
The following subsections define the exact shapes of five of the eight
core record families. `SemanticObject`, `TypedRelation`, `Constraint`,
`Latitude` and `Residual` populate `O`, `E`, `C`, `L` and `X`. The
traversal record (§5), the transformation record (AC-013) and the judgment
record (AC-014) populate `V`, `T` and `J`. A traversal, transformation or
judgment is not placed in `O` merely by reifying its name as a semantic
object. A subject model may independently represent the concept of a
record kind, but that representation does not satisfy the core population
law (P3, P1).

constraints.statement: SemanticObject, TypedRelation, Constraint, Latitude and Residual populate O/E/C/L/X; traversal, transformation and judgment populate V/T/J. Reifying a record-kind name as an object does not place an operational record in O or satisfy its required core population. Independently representing record-kind concepts is permitted but distinct.

grounding.quote:
`kind` resolves one declared `ConstraintKind`; `judgment_kind` resolves
one declared `JudgmentKind`. The owning signature defines the predicate
language and how its result is judged. A predicate that is not
deterministically decidable states the required probabilistic or human
judgment kind rather than pretending to be a machine proof (P6, P1).

constraints.statement: Declare the required probabilistic or human judgment kind instead of claiming machine proof. Both constraint and judgment kinds must resolve within the owning signature.
conditions: A predicate is not deterministically decidable.

grounding.quote:
Projection, compression, interpretation or encoding cannot erase a
residual. It remains represented, is explicitly dispositioned by competent
authority, or causes refusal (P4b, P6).

`kind` resolves one declared `ResidualKind`. The owning signature defines
its lawful subject, uncertainty, consequence, re-entry and invalidation
domains. An undeclared residual kind or value refuses structural admission
(P3).

constraints.statement: Projection, compression, interpretation and encoding cannot erase residuals: retain them, record competent disposition or refuse. Undeclared residual kinds or values refuse structural admission.
exceptions: Competent authority explicitly dispositions the residual.

grounding.quote:
Every admitted object, relation, constraint, latitude, residual,
traversal, transformation specialisation and judgment belongs to one
declared signature. Every fundamental record also occurs exactly once in
the total `Population_M` function under its declared `RecordKind_ac`.
Missing, duplicate, shadowed or unknown record kinds and populations fail
closed (P3, P5).

constraints.statement: Every admitted fundamental record belongs to one declared signature and occurs exactly once under its declared core kind in total Population_M. Missing, duplicate, shadowed or unknown kinds/populations fail closed.

grounding.quote:
So an identity resolves one member under one type,
context, owner, scope and basis. That equal representations do not
establish equal meaning is FOUNDATIONS §2, Representation. The `a_c`
binding beside it: equal spelling, payload equality, position in any
structure and carrier equality do not establish semantic identity (P3).

constraints.statement: Every identity in I resolves one member under one type, context, owner, scope and basis. Owner maps to authority, type to kind, resolved member to denoted value; context/scope/basis are additional required coordinates permitted by IDENTITY §2. Equal spelling, payload, structural position or carrier does not establish semantic identity.

grounding.quote:
Every referenced identity resolves exactly once in the applicable model or
through one explicit external relation. Resolution uses the exact
`RefDomain_Sigma(source_record_kind, field)` declaration across the
model's record populations. Dangling, duplicate, wrong-record-kind,
wrong-sort, wrong-basis, locally-and-externally ambiguous or
undeclared-field references refuse structural admission (P3, P5).

constraints.statement: Every reference resolves exactly once locally or through one explicit external relation using its exact RefDomain_Sigma declaration. Dangling, duplicate, wrong-kind, wrong-sort, wrong-basis, local/external ambiguous and undeclared-field references refuse structural admission; AC-007 separately determines the refusal's core value by cause.

grounding.quote:
A relation is lawful only when its kind admits the exact source and target
sorts and all required qualifiers are present. Direction is material
unless the relation kind explicitly declares symmetry (P4a, P3).

constraints.statement: Lawfulness requires exact admitted endpoint sorts and all required qualifiers; direction is material subject to explicit symmetry.
exceptions: Direction is immaterial only when the relation kind explicitly declares symmetry.

grounding.quote:
Objects, relations, constraints, latitude, residuals, traversals,
transformations, projections and judgments retain their declared semantic,
operation, evaluation and decision authority (the kinds of
[FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds)). What
creates no authority is listed there; in `a_c` its instances are copying,
interpreting, encoding, evaluating and transporting a record, none of
which transfers authority (P6, P4b).

constraints.statement: All listed records and projections retain declared semantic, operation, evaluation and decision authority. Copying, interpreting, encoding, evaluating or transporting transfers none.

grounding.quote:
Every result binds its exact basis under
[RF-005](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-005-exact-basis-and-coordinates), which
owns the exact-basis rule for results; what a basis is, including that
mixed bases need an explicit composite relation, is FOUNDATIONS §2,
Basis. This law binds the same rule to every fundamental record and model
of `a_c`: each binds an exact basis, the composite-basis relation of a
mixed basis is an explicitly owned record, and individually valid
coordinates do not create a coherent composite basis by proximity (P6, P3).

constraints.statement: Every result, fundamental record and model binds an exact basis. Individually valid nearby coordinates do not constitute coherent composite basis. FOUNDATIONS defines Basis and RF-005 owns result exactness; AC-006 applies it to records/models.
exceptions: Mixed bases require an explicit owned composite-basis record.

grounding.quote:
A missing result is no value of this refinement: a judgment that was not
performed has no closed result, is never `indeterminate`, and enters every
conjunction over it as a planned assessment without a closed result
(FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, Not performed).

constraints.statement: For the predicate that the constraint holds for its governed subject on exact basis: holds→satisfied with established predicate; failed→falsified with named counterexample; undecidable admissible evidence→indeterminate naming deciding evidence; outside applies_to/context/scope requiring an undeclared relation→out_of_frame naming that relation and source-given owner; unsupported subject/basis→invalid_basis naming repair. No mapping raises standing or coerces failure, absence, indeterminacy, out-of-scope or invalid basis to satisfied. A judgment not performed has no closed result, is not indeterminate and enters conjunction as planned assessment without a result.
conditions: A constraint judgment is performed.

grounding.quote: | `hold` | indeterminate | the operation was applied and stops because evidence, an observation or a disposition it needs is not yet admitted, so the admissible evidence cannot decide whether it yields its result; its residual names what would decide |

constraints.statement: For the predicate that the operation yields its declared result on exact basis: declared result→satisfied, establishing availability of a proposed model/successor only, not acceptance/admission; hold→indeterminate when required evidence/observation/disposition is not yet admitted, naming what decides; gap→invalid_basis when a needed member/reference/resolution/declaration remains unresolved by its declared relation; refusal(constraint)→falsified for a demonstrated law/signature violation by what is judged or any refusal not naming a basis condition; refusal(basis)→invalid_basis for basis conditions without a demonstrated violation by what is judged. A resolved-to-no-target local/external reference is dangling and refuses, distinct from open external resolution. Basis-only causes include inexact seeds/relations/edge semantics/basis/scope, nonfinite/nonunique fixed points, unestablished input identity/basis/admission or mixed bases without composite relation. Refusal names its condition, admits no record/model/carrier and silently drops nothing.
conditions: A closure, projection, structural admission, transformation application or interpretation is applied.

grounding.quote:
A basis mismatch inside a model or a record, a
relation's qualifier record included, is mixed bases with no
composite-basis relation (AC-006): a coordinate of the model or record
binds, or a reference in it resolves on, a basis that the governing basis
relation does not admit, as a wrong-basis reference of AC-003 does. It is
a condition of the basis, in the structural admission that judges that
model or record as in every other operation, and never a violated
constraint of a signature, even where the signature declares the basis
relation; a refusal that names only such a mismatch is `refusal(basis)`.

constraints.statement: Cause is part of refusal value. A demonstrated violation by the judged record/model/carrier/transformation/application makes refusal(constraint), even with a basis condition; report the latter alongside as a separate invalid_basis result naming repair and the unsupported evaluation predicate, not the operation-outcome predicate. Known failure/counterexample survives conjunction. A defect in an input used as basis is a basis condition for that operation. Basis mismatch—including qualifier or wrong-basis reference—is always a basis condition, never signature-constraint violation, even when the signature declares the basis relation. Thus AC-001 violation may falsify model admission while invalidating the basis of projection over that model. Unapplied operations have no outcome. A gap stop is a closed invalid_basis result, distinct from missing-result conjunction gaps. Signature/traversal-specific stops map under §5. Unestablished closure/projection is invalid_basis for its predicate, as closure_unresolved is for its own activation predicate.

grounding.quote:
Two values may differ lawfully only through an applicable latitude record
or transformation relation. An implementation preference, a probabilistic
choice or a human presence is not implicit latitude. FOUNDATIONS §4 states
the same rule for any two values; this law is its form over `L` and `T`
(P6, P1).

constraints.statement: Lawful differences require declared applicable latitude or transformation. Implementation preference, probabilistic choice and human presence supply no implicit latitude.
exceptions: An applicable latitude record or transformation relation permits the difference.

grounding.quote:
Every material uncertainty, omission, translation loss, unresolved
boundary or unproven relation remains in `X` until an authorised
disposition creates an exact successor model. Absence from a projection is
not resolution (P4b).

constraints.statement: Every material uncertainty, omission, translation loss, unresolved boundary and unproved relation remains in X until authorised successor disposition. Projection absence is not resolution.
exceptions: Authorised disposition creates an exact successor model.

grounding.quote:
The result is defined only when `Z`, `R`, required-edge semantics, basis
and scope are exact and the fixed point is finite and unique. Failure to
establish those conditions returns a gap or refusal: `gap` where a
condition is unresolved on the basis, otherwise `refusal(basis)`, because
each condition bears on the basis the closure acts on (AC-007). Least
closure means least lawful record closure under `R`; it does not claim
globally minimal prose, bytes, tokens, cost or cognitive effort.
ACTIVATION §2 applies this closure to the construction of a step's context
under an envelope.

constraints.statement: Closure exists only with exact Z/R/required-edge semantics/basis/scope and finite unique fixed point. Unresolved required conditions return gap; otherwise failure to establish them returns refusal(basis). Least lawful closure claims no global minimum prose, bytes, tokens, cost or cognition. ACTIVATION §2 applies it to step context under an envelope.

grounding.quote:
A
projection is not a new semantic owner. It is a reference, so the rule
that no reference trims a required member to fit a carrier or budget,
stated at [FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra), Reference versus
body, applies to it: here the required members are those of the material
closure of `Z`, and a capability budget is one such budget. ACTIVATION §2
applies the projection to a step's context, and every projected frame of
this corpus is one.

constraints.statement: Projection preserves selected meaning and contains closure with explicit seams. Failures inherited from closure/input model are gap or refusal(basis). It creates no semantic owner and may not trim required closure members for carrier, capability or other budgets. Step contexts and this corpus's projected frames are applications of this projection.

grounding.quote:
Override,
disambiguation, equivalence, specialisation or translation exists only as
a typed relation with exact authority, direction, scope, basis,
preservation, loss, refusal and invalidation semantics (P3, P6).

constraints.statement: Overlay cannot mutate its basis. Override, disambiguation, equivalence, specialisation and translation require typed relations with exact authority, direction, scope, basis, preservation, loss, refusal and invalidation semantics.

grounding.quote:
`domain_model` and `codomain_model` resolve exact content identities of
the complete input and proposed successor models. Each model identity
commits to its exact calculus basis, signature identity, complete finite
`Population_M`, complete `External_M`, exact external-resolution map and
selected model-content identity under the owning identity law. A mutable
locator, a model-family name, a partial projection or a population digest
without the exact model identity refuses (P3).

constraints.statement: t.traversal resolves one exact v; context, owner, scope, basis, operation authority, evidence, provenance and stop contract equal or lawfully restrict v, otherwise refuse. Domain/codomain identify complete exact models committing to calculus basis, signature, full populations/external identities/resolution map and owned content identity; mutable locators, family names, partial projections or population digests alone refuse. Ordinary transformations share domain/codomain/t/traversal basis and domain/codomain signature. Migration needs the stated separate specialisation. Changed basis or record kind forces removal/introduction and continuity only through exact migration, never preserved membership. Preservation_relation is exact typed equality binding both models/bases, record kinds, comparison domain, direction, authority, scope, evidence and equality law; equivalence/meaning preservation may relate removed/introduction but cannot preserve an identity.
exceptions: Cross-basis/signature migration has a separately identified specialisation with exact composite-basis and compatible signature-extension relations naming both sides.

grounding.quote:
Local_b       = P_t disjoint_union R_t
Local_b_prime = P_t disjoint_union N_t
N_t intersect Local_b = empty
R_t intersect Local_b_prime = empty

constraints.statement: Prove Local_b = P_t disjoint_union R_t; Local_b_prime = P_t disjoint_union N_t; N_t intersects no input identity and R_t no successor identity. Preserved records retain exact kind, identity, context, owner, scope and basis, with either byte identity under one exact shared canonical grammar or exact typed equality when no shared byte grammar exists. These are alternative proofs, not carrier selection. Changed fields/basis/kind, nominal identifier equality, equivalence or unbound preservation assertions refuse P_t. Every input identity is classified exactly once; every introduction is a complete lawful record in exactly one successor population; removals are absent. No silent dropping, retention or duplication.
conditions: A lawful transformation is claimed.

grounding.quote:
The two resolution tuples are exactly field-equal. A nominally equal
external identifier, an equivalent target, a changed target kind, a
changed resolved target, a changed reference domain, a changed basis
relation, a changed resolution basis or a missing witness cannot enter
`EP_t`. Every member of `ER_t` has its complete resolution only in the
domain model; every member of `EN_t` has its complete resolution only in
the codomain model. A changed external resolution is a removal followed by
introduction of the new resolution coordinate and any separately declared
continuity relation; the referenced external identity may remain
unchanged, but the resolution is not preserved. Witnesses are total and
unique over `EP_t` and name no other resolution coordinate (P4b, P3).

constraints.statement: Every external identity has exactly one exact resolution tuple; missing/ambiguous/extra tuples refuse. Prove E_b = EP_t disjoint_union ER_t; E_b_prime = EP_t disjoint_union EN_t; EN_t intersects no E_b and ER_t no E_b_prime. Each preserved tuple has exactly one total, exclusive witness binding both models/resolutions, equal decision and evidence, with field-exact equality. Nominal identity, equivalent targets, changes to target kind/target/reference domain/basis relation/resolution basis or missing witnesses cannot preserve. Removed tuples occur only in input, introduced only in successor. Changed resolution requires removal/introduction and separate continuity even if referenced external identity remains unchanged.
conditions: A lawful transformation is claimed.

grounding.quote:
Material residuals remain in the successor residual set unless an exact
authorised disposition is included in the transformation evidence.
Failure to establish any model identity, basis, population, local or
external partition, equality, external-resolution witness, residual or
codomain equation refuses (P4b, P5).

constraints.statement: Retain material residuals in successors absent exact authorised evidence of disposition. Failure of any identity, basis, population, local/external partition, equality, resolution witness, residual or codomain equation refuses. Exact t declares every permitted mutation; input stays unchanged, successor is merely proposed and cannot accept/admit itself. Stops map by AC-007 cause. FOUNDATIONS consumes preserved/introduced/removed records, resolution witnesses and residuals as conservation accounting.
exceptions: An exact authorised residual disposition is included in transformation evidence.

grounding.quote:
Issuing a judgment does not transform, rewrite, reissue or rename its
subject. Promotion is an explicit relation between the unchanged subject
and its admission or acceptance judgment (P6, P3).

constraints.statement: Judgment issuance never transforms, rewrites, reissues or renames the subject. Promotion is a separate explicit relation from unchanged subject to its admission/acceptance judgment.

grounding.quote:
Each refined value, whether the stop contract or a
`stop_states` declares it, names its parent value and its cause and maps
to its parent's core value: a value refined from `hold` to indeterminate,
from `gap` or `refusal(basis)` to invalid_basis, and from
`refusal(constraint)` to falsified. No refined value takes `satisfied`.

constraints.statement: Each stop maps to exactly one existing core value, never satisfied. Further stops declare their single core mapping in the signature stop contract; traversal stop_states binds its exact mapping. Every refinement names parent and cause and keeps the parent's core value: hold -> indeterminate; gap and refusal(basis) -> invalid_basis; refusal(constraint) -> falsified. A different core value requires a different parent declared only by that parent's owning member; this member owns the four named stops. Neither contract nor stop_states raises standing or turns a violated constraint into mere evidential undecidability.
constraints.uncertainty: The full cause definitions in AC-007 are outside the supplied sections.
conditions: For every stop value and each cause refinement declared by the signature stop contract or traversal stop_states.

grounding.quote:
Every functor application binds exactly one functor kind and one traversal
identity. Applying any `F_*` kind without the bracketed traversal identity
`[v]` is incomplete (P3). Such an
application violates this law, and its outcome is `refusal(constraint)`
under AC-007; this sense of incomplete is not the construction-availability
value `incomplete` of a step

constraints.statement: Bind exactly one kind and one traversal identity. An F_* application lacking bracketed [v] violates AC-015 and yields refusal(constraint), whose supplied core mapping is falsified. Its descriptive incompleteness is not ACTIVATION's construction-availability value incomplete.
constraints.uncertainty: ACTIVATION's separate incomplete value is referenced but not defined here.
conditions: For every functor application.

grounding.quote:
"Functor kind" is an `a_c` term for this traversal classification. It does
not by itself assert a category-theoretic functor. A model that claims
categorical functor laws carries the demonstration that
[FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra), Formal fragment, requires of
every categorical claim (P6, P1).

constraints.statement: Functor-kind classification alone makes no category-theoretic assertion. A categorical claim carries the required Formal fragment demonstration; the supplied conformance discriminator further requires objects, arrows, arrow equality, identity, composition and demonstrated functor laws before such a claim.
constraints.uncertainty: FOUNDATIONS' full formal requirements are not supplied.
conditions: If a model claims categorical functor laws.

grounding.quote:
The proposed model `M_subject*` does not become accepted through
construction. Structural evaluation can prove closed shape, reference
typing, identity derivation and basis coherence. It cannot prove that
probabilistic semantic selection retained every material subject meaning.

constraints.statement: The contract makes FOUNDATIONS §2 Interpretation exact for one subject and signature and declares every listed coordinate: exact calculus basis; subject identity, inventory and bytes or semantic addresses; signature and compatible extension; mapping to every applicable record population, including the eight named populations; interpreter identity, capability, provenance and stops; structural evaluation; semantic selection and acceptance authority; source re-entry and invalidation. Construction grants no acceptance. Structural proof of shape, references, identity or basis does not establish retention of every material meaning; semantic acceptance remains separate.
constraints.uncertainty: The cited FOUNDATIONS definition and full source-defined record schemas are absent.
conditions: For an exact-subject interpretation contract.

grounding.quote:
Every admitted model record maps to exact subject provenance or is
explicitly identified as model-local content under competent authority.
Every evaluated subject declaration has a retained, omitted, residual,
inapplicable or refused disposition. Interpretation cannot treat absence
as immateriality without a recorded basis and authority (P1, P4b, P6).

constraints.statement: Admitted records require exact subject provenance or the stated model-local exception. Every evaluated declaration receives retained, omitted, residual, inapplicable or refused disposition. Absence cannot be treated as immaterial without recorded basis and authority.
conditions: For every admitted model record and every evaluated subject declaration.
exceptions: A record may be explicitly model-local under competent authority instead of mapping to exact subject provenance.

grounding.quote:
The separation of structural conformance from semantic fidelity, and the
rule that structural success is evidence for semantic review and no
substitute for it, are [EVALUATION §2](EVALUATION.md#2-separation)'s,
which owns them for every review.

constraints.statement: Keep structural conformance separate from semantic fidelity. Structural success supports semantic review but cannot substitute for it; the owning rule remains EVALUATION's.
constraints.uncertainty: EVALUATION's wider review protocol is unavailable in these sections.
conditions: For every review, as owned by EVALUATION §2 and bound here to a_c.

grounding.quote:
Encoding requires `J_X.decision = accepted` and exact equality between the
judgment subject identity and digest and `M_X`; hold or refusal cannot be
encoded.

`accepted` and
`admitted` map to satisfied, a hold maps as AC-007's `hold`, and `refuse`
is a `refusal` that takes its core value under AC-007 by its cause

constraints.statement: Encoding requires an accepted J_X whose subject identity and digest exactly equal unchanged M_X; hold and refusal cannot be encoded. Acceptance and admission answer distinct predicates, do not alter subject identity, and combine with other results only through core mappings: accepted/admitted -> satisfied; hold -> AC-007 hold; refuse -> cause-dependent AC-007 refusal. Withheld or refused judgments never count as accepted.
conditions: When encoding a model or combining semantic-acceptance and carrier-admission results.

grounding.quote:
`a_c`, `a_c.X` and `a_c.X.C` have independent content identities,
judgments, supersession relations and proof obligations (P3, P6):

An encoding failure does not change `a_c.X`. An interpretation failure
does not change `a_c`. A downstream success cannot ratify an upstream
layer or basis. None of these layers is automatically an independently
released Product.

constraints.statement: The three layers retain independent content identities, judgments, supersession and proof obligations. Calculus qualification tests internal coherence against its complete declared laws; interpretation proves fidelity to exact X; carrier qualification proves faithful canonical encoding of the accepted model. Encoding failure does not change the interpreted model, interpretation failure does not change the calculus, and downstream success cannot ratify upstream basis or layer. Product status belongs to an external authority selecting and releasing the layer, never follows automatically. SPEC_METHOD §6 applies this law to release lineage.
constraints.uncertainty: SPEC_METHOD's release-lineage application is not supplied.

grounding.quote:
kind: "stdo.axiomatic-calculus-basis",
  schema_version: 1,
  concept_identity: "urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:a-c",

The record uses RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme bytes. Duplicate
object names are rejected before canonicalisation.
`derivation_basis.principle_refs` is duplicate-free and sorted by
ascending unsigned UTF-16 code units.

constraints.statement: The record has kind stdo.axiomatic-calculus-basis, schema_version 1 and concept_identity urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:a-c. derivation_basis contains an absolute immutable package release_uri, manifest_sha256 and nonempty absolute semantic-address principle_refs. publication_basis contains the same release_uri, manifest_sha256, absolute member_uri within that release and member_sha256. Each digest field is 'sha256:' plus 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Reject duplicate object names before RFC 8785 JCS canonicalisation; principle_refs is duplicate-free and sorted ascending by unsigned UTF-16 code units. Identity is urn:stdo:axiomatic-calculus-basis:sha256: followed by sha256(JCS(AxiomaticCalculusBasis)).
constraints.uncertainty: No basis record is constructed or its identity calculated here.
conditions: For the source-defined AxiomaticCalculusBasis record.

grounding.quote:
A principle reference outside the bound package, a
missing or ambiguous clause, an extra undeclared premise reference, or a
manifest or member digest mismatch invalidates the record (P3, P6).

The identity record is external to the member bytes and to the manifest
member set whose digest it names. It is issued only after that set and its
manifest are frozen

constraints.statement: derivation_basis binds the complete finite governing-clause set identified by §1 Derivation provenance; recompute it when clauses change, never infer it from a hard-coded member count. Every reference resolves within publication_basis's exact package, with equal release_uri and manifest_sha256 across both roles; co-publication does not transfer premise ownership. publication_basis binds exact member bytes at a member_uri within its release. Every release_uri has immutable stdo://releases/v<version>-rc.<positive-ordinal>/ form. Acceptance is a verdict over that cut, not another identity; record presence grants no acceptance or release status. Outside-package references, missing/ambiguous clauses, extra undeclared premises and digest mismatches invalidate the record. Issue only after frozen member set and manifest; keep the record outside both hashed member set and member bytes. It may accompany them as external metadata, but neither member nor manifest embeds its identity or final bytes. The record hashes already-fixed coordinates without reverse dependency.
constraints.uncertainty: The actual §1 premise inventory and RELEASE issuance/acceptance rules are not supplied.

grounding.quote:
id(a_c.X) binds
  exact id(a_c)
  + exact subject basis id(X)
  + exact interpretation contract
  + selected model content identity
  + semantic-selection ledger identity and digest

id(a_c.X.C) binds
  exact id(a_c.X)
  + exact carrier Product or cut
  + exact encoding profile
  + canonical carrier content identity

A dependency on a released calculus binds that record's identity,
release, manifest digest and member digest. A mutable authoring copy or an
unissued record is never substituted for that exact basis (P3, P6).

constraints.statement: Interpreted identity binds at least exact calculus identity, subject basis identity, interpretation contract, selected model content identity and semantic-selection ledger identity/digest. Carrier identity binds at least exact interpreted identity, carrier Product or cut, encoding profile and canonical carrier content identity. Semantic acceptance points to unchanged interpreted identity/digest and stays external to both identities; encoding mechanically verifies that match and retains acceptance as evidence. Admission points to unchanged carrier identity/digest; admitted encoding is the external triple (a_c.X.C, J_X, D_C). Product acceptance/release likewise point to content-first identities. The owning Product defines downstream canonical grammar and issuance authority but cannot omit upstream identities or replace them with mutable locators. Publication binding is issued under RELEASE and AC-020 after exact package bytes exist, tying this member and §1 governing clauses to the same package. Released-calculus dependencies bind the issued record's identity, release, manifest and member digests; mutable authoring copies and unissued records cannot substitute.
constraints.uncertainty: Downstream canonical grammars and issuance authorities are intentionally delegated and not specified here.
conditions: For downstream identities and dependencies on a released calculus.

grounding.quote:
This member defines the generic relations `a_c.X` and `a_c.X.C`. It
selects, constructs, accepts or releases no concrete interpretation or
carrier. A downstream authority owns its exact subject population,
interpretation, carrier, judgments and Product or release status. The
downstream identity is never embedded back into the calculus or its
publication basis (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: The member defines generic interpretation and carrier relations without selecting, constructing, accepting or releasing concrete instances. Downstream authority owns exact subject population, interpretation, carrier, judgments and Product/release status. Downstream identity is never embedded back in the calculus or publication basis.

grounding.quote:
The task's declared subject and work boundary
are the seed set `Z`, with the dependency relation family `R` the task
declares, and the surface is `project(M_subject, Z, R)` (AC-011) over the
material closure of AC-010.

constraints.statement: Use task subject/work boundary as seed Z and its declared dependency family R: project(M_subject,Z,R) under AC-011 over AC-010 material closure. Surface objects/meanings come from M_Z semantic objects with AC-002 identity and AC-017 provenance; predicates/dependencies from constraints and typed relations under AC-007/AC-004, sharing one premise record across several constraints without imposing tree shape or execution order; operations from closure traversals/transformations with preconditions and operation authority; results from constraint judgment kinds/outcomes mapped under AC-007; freedom from AC-008 latitude; authority retained per record under AC-005, with none granted by the surface; evidence from judgments and evidence/provenance/basis under AC-014/AC-006; unresolved conditions from AC-009 residuals and AC-011 Boundary_Z seams.
constraints.uncertainty: Full closure, projection, transformation and record laws referenced by the construction are absent.
conditions: For a task projection from an interpreted subject.

grounding.quote:
A missing premise or an omitted
   obligation never becomes permission or a satisfied result (AC-007,
   AC-009).

It
   supplies no observation, effect grant or task context

constraints.statement: Preserve each element's recorded standing as premise, derived consequence, policy choice, observation or unresolved claim; retain policy ownership and never turn preference into obligation. Construction/assurance elements keep their recorded kind among FOUNDATIONS' five support kinds: formula is not discharge, and externally assessed predicates retain establishing source, scope and evidence. A residual, hold, gap or unestablished external predicate retains source and required acquisition and blocks every dependent operation/result until its premise is established. Missing premises and omitted obligations grant neither permission nor satisfaction. A surface carries constraints and acquisition routes, not observations, effect grants or task context; ACTIVATION §2 acquisition obtains those from workspace and selected authoritative inputs, and workspace remains the reacquisition basis.
constraints.uncertainty: The five support-kind definitions and detailed acquisition protocol are not supplied.
conditions: Whenever a constraint surface is used.

grounding.quote:
